another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my little boy Alex. He's four years old. I was wondering if I could claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To start, could you please tell me: **Are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does he live with you, and are you the person who is responsible for his day-to-day care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does live with me, but... actually, his mum also lives with us and she's already claiming Child Benefit for him. I help look after him of course, but she's the one who gets the payments.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. This is an important detail.

Just to clarify: **Are you and Alex's mum living together as a couple in the same household, or are you living in the same house but in a different arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we're living together as a couple - it's just the three of us in the household.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

This is helpful information. In your situation, where you and Alex's mum are living together as a couple in the same household with Alex, and she is already claiming Child Benefit for him, there are specific rules that apply.

Let me ask one more question to ensure I have the complete picture: **Is there any particular reason you're looking to claim Child Benefit for Alex yourself, or any change in circumstances that's prompting this inquiry?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I was just curious really. I wasn't sure how it all worked - whether we could both claim or if I should be the one claiming instead. I just wanted to understand if I'm eligible or if there's anything I should be doing differently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying - that makes perfect sense, and it's good that you're checking to understand how it all works.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me explain the situation:

You are living with Alex's mum as a couple in the same household, and she is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Under Child Benefit rules, **only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child**. When two people are both responsible for a child and live together in the same household, only one of them can claim - you cannot both receive Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be eligible to also claim for him while this arrangement continues. The current setup where she receives the payments is perfectly fine as long as one of you is claiming.

However, it's worth noting that if circumstances were to change (for example, if you and Alex's mum were to separate and Alex lived primarily with you), then you could potentially become the claimant instead.
